stem: What is the difference between a class and an object?

options.content: A class is a template; an object is an instance of it
options.rationale: The class defines properties and methods; the object holds values.

options.content: A class is one item; an object is a template
A class holds the data; an object holds only the methods
options.rationale: An object holds its own data.

options.content: They mean the same thing
options.rationale: A class is a type; an object is an instance.

explanation: A class is a blueprint; an object is an instance of it.

stem: What is the purpose of encapsulation?

options.content: To hide the data and allow access only through methods
To allow every part of a program to change the data directly
To let a new class reuse an existing class
To give the same method different behaviour in different classes

explanation: Encapsulation = private data + public methods.

stem: What does a subclass receive from its superclass through inheritance?

options.content: Its properties and methods, which it can add to or override
options.rationale: A subclass reuses and extends what the superclass defines.

options.content: Nothing, because the subclass must define everything again
Only the objects that were created from the superclass
Only the private data of one object
options.rationale: Inheritance applies to the class, not to one object.

explanation: A subclass inherits the superclass's properties and methods.

stem: Which relationship between two classes is best described by containment (aggregation) rather than inheritance?

options.content: A `Nurse` is a kind of `Employee`
A `Bus` is a kind of `Vehicle`
A `Dvd` is a kind of `Item`
A `Clinic` has many `Patient` objects
options.rationale: A clinic has patients as parts; it is not a kind of patient.

explanation: Use the test "has a" for containment and "is a" for inheritance.
hints: Which pair of classes fits the sentence 'X has a Y'?

stem: What is a constructor?

options.content: A method that deletes an object when it is no longer needed
A property that cannot be changed
A class that has no subclasses
A method that runs when an object is created
options.rationale: In pseudocode it is called NEW.

explanation: The constructor initialises a new object.

stem: What is meant by overriding a method?

options.content: Two classes share one method with the same code and cannot change it
options.rationale: That is simple inheritance, not overriding.

options.content: A method is made private so it cannot be used
A subclass supplies its own version of a method it inherits
options.rationale: The subclass method replaces the superclass version for its objects.

options.content: An object is deleted and created again
options.rationale: That has nothing to do with methods.

explanation: Overriding redefines an inherited method in the subclass.
hints: Which class supplies the new version of the method?

stem: A program calls `Print()` on a `Circle` object and on a `Square` object, and each draws a different shape. This is an example of

options.content: encapsulation
polymorphism
options.rationale: One method name, different behaviour by class.

options.content: containment
instantiation

explanation: Polymorphism: the same call behaves differently for different classes.
hints: The same method name does different things in different classes.

stem: Which is a benefit of object-oriented programming?

options.content: Programs always run much faster than any other style
Programs need no testing because classes cannot have errors
Classes can be reused and extended by inheritance
No design is needed beforehand

explanation: Reuse and easier maintenance are benefits of OOP.

stem: In an inheritance relationship, the subclass is a more specialised kind of the superclass.
explanation: True. A Bus is a kind of Vehicle; it has all the properties and methods of a Vehicle plus its own.

stem: If the properties of a class are made public, code outside the class cannot change them.
explanation: False. Public properties can be read and changed from anywhere. To protect them they must be private.

stem: Complete the sentences by choosing the correct term.

payload.template:
A {{blank:a}} is a template for objects.

A procedure or function that belongs to a class is called a {{blank:b}}.

A data item held by an object is a {{blank:c}}.

explanation: A class is a template; a method is a routine of the class; a property is a data item.

stem: A fleet has one `Vehicle`, one `Kombi` and one `Bus`. The `Vehicle` method `DailyCost` returns 10. The `Kombi` overrides it to return the superclass value plus 5, and the `Bus` overrides it to return the superclass value multiplied by 3. State the total of the three daily costs.
explanation: The total is 55.
hints: Work out the daily cost of each kind of vehicle from its method.

stem: State the term for creating an object from a class.
explanation: Creating an object from a class is instantiation.

stem: Match each term to its meaning.

right.content: The same method name behaves differently in different classes
An object has another object as one of its properties
Data is private and accessed through methods
A subclass reuses the properties and methods of a superclass

explanation: The four ideas of an object-oriented design.

stem: Explain how encapsulation protects the balance of a bank account object. [3]

points.description: The balance property is private, so other code cannot change it directly
It can be changed only through public methods such as deposit and withdraw
These methods can check the data (for example reject a negative deposit or an overdraft) so the balance stays valid

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The balance is a private property, so other code cannot change it directly. It can be changed only through public methods such as deposit and withdraw, which check the data and reject invalid amounts.

explanation: Private data + checking methods.
hints: Give a reason, a how, and an example.

stem: A school system holds learners and teachers. Both have a name and an ID number; a learner also has a form and a teacher has a subject. Describe a class design that uses inheritance. [4]

points.description: A superclass such as Person with the properties Name and ID
A subclass Learner that inherits from Person and adds Form
A subclass Teacher that inherits from Person and adds Subject
The shared properties are defined once, so they are not repeated in the subclasses

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Person is the superclass with the properties Name and ID. Learner inherits from Person and adds Form. Teacher inherits from Person and adds Subject. The shared properties are written once in Person.

explanation: Move shared properties to a superclass.
hints: Put the shared properties in the superclass.

stem: State three benefits of using an object-oriented approach to write a large program. [3]

points.description: Inheritance allows code to be reused
Encapsulation protects data from accidental change
Classes can be tested and maintained separately (or model real-world things, making the design easier to understand)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Inheritance lets code be reused, encapsulation protects data from accidental change, and each class can be tested and maintained separately.

explanation: Reuse, protection and maintenance.
hints: Think of reuse, protection of data and maintenance.

stem: Distinguish between inheritance and containment, using the classes `Car`, `Engine` and `Vehicle` as examples. [3]

points.description: Inheritance is an "is a" relationship: a Car is a kind of Vehicle, so Car can inherit from Vehicle
Containment is a "has a" relationship: a Car has an Engine, so a Car object contains an Engine object as a property
A Car does not inherit from Engine, because it is not a kind of engine

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Inheritance is an is-a relationship: Car is a kind of Vehicle, so Car inherits from Vehicle. Containment is a has-a relationship: a Car has an Engine, so the Car object holds an Engine object as a property.

explanation: Is-a versus has-a.
hints: Use the words 'is a' and 'has a'.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Which class is the superclass in the program?

options.content: `Kombi`
options.rationale: Kombi is a subclass of Vehicle.

options.content: `Vehicle`
options.rationale: Kombi and Bus both inherit from Vehicle.

options.content: `Bus`
options.rationale: Bus is a subclass of Vehicle.

options.content: `fleet`
options.rationale: fleet is a list of objects, not a class.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: State the third line of output.
parts.explanation: For the Bus, daily_cost is 10 × 3 = 30 and label is inherited.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Identify the method that is overridden in this program and explain what is shown by the fact that the same call `v.daily_cost()` gives different values.

points.description: daily_cost is overridden (in Kombi and Bus)
This is polymorphism: the same method call behaves differently depending on the class of the object

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: daily_cost is overridden in Kombi and Bus. The same call gives different values for different objects, which is polymorphism.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Give one reason why `label` is not written again in the `Kombi` and `Bus` classes.

points.description: It is inherited from Vehicle, so the code is reused

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: It is inherited from Vehicle, so the code does not have to be repeated.

explanation: Reading an inheritance program and its output.
hints: Read the program top to bottom: which class defines each method?
The loop calls the same method on each object.

stem: A clinic in Masvingo wants a program that stores its patients and staff. Every person has a name and a phone number. A patient also has a date of birth, and a nurse has a ward. The clinic keeps a list of the patients it is treating, and each patient has a medical record that holds the diagnosis and the treatment.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Identify a suitable superclass and two subclasses and state one property of each of the three classes.

points.description: Superclass Person (with the properties Name and Phone)
Subclasses Patient (DateOfBirth) and Nurse (Ward)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Person (Name, Phone) is the superclass; Patient (DateOfBirth) and Nurse (Ward) are its subclasses.

parts.explanation: Shared properties go in the superclass.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: State the relationship between the classes `Patient` and `MedicalRecord` and justify it.

points.description: Containment (aggregation), a has-a relationship
A patient has a medical record; a patient is not a kind of record, so inheritance is wrong

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Containment: a patient has a medical record. A patient is not a kind of record, so inheritance would not fit.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Which property of `Patient` should be private to protect it?

options.content: The name of the class
options.rationale: A class name is not a property.

options.content: The keyword NEW
options.rationale: NEW is the constructor, not a property.

options.content: The diagnosis in the medical record
options.rationale: Medical information is sensitive and should be accessed only through checked methods.

options.content: The length of the list of patients
options.rationale: The size of a list does not need protection in the same way.

parts.explanation: Private properties are changed only through methods that check the data.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Explain how polymorphism could be used when the clinic prints a badge for each person.

points.description: Each class (Person, Patient, Nurse) has a method such as PrintBadge, overridden to show its own details
One loop can call PrintBadge on every object in a list and each prints the right badge

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Each class has its own version of PrintBadge. A loop calls PrintBadge on every object in a list and each object prints the correct badge.

explanation: Designing classes for a clinic system.
hints: The class design is a table of properties and methods.
Decide which relationship is 'is a' and which is 'has a'.
